summary: Final tokens missing after edge connection coalescence during stream resume
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Clipstream reports that when their web client experiences a short network hiccup and the SSE connection resumes, the final portion of the streamed response (last ~5–20 tokens / the closing punctuation) is not delivered to the client. The model completes generation on the server side (server logs show full output) but the client never receives the terminal fragments.

Impact:
- Affects 3 Clipstream production endpoints; manifests intermittently (~1 in 300 resumed streams)
- Causes truncated captions and missing closing punctuation in user-facing transcripts
- Customer is on Dedicated tier and needs deterministic delivery for live captioning

Environment:
- prod | us-east-1 behind our edge-proxy fleet (nginx-based custom layer)
- Dedicated serving-host pool for Clipstream with pinned redwood-open-7b model

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Start a long streaming session with SSE from the Clipstream app to Redwood hosted endpoint
2) Simulate a short network drop on the client (100–500 ms) causing SSE reconnect
3) Observe resumed stream in browser: final sentence sometimes missing; stream ends without explicit "end" event

Observed behavior:
- Server-side traces show generator finished and emitted terminal metadata (choice.finish_reason = "stop")
- Edge-proxy access logs show two adjacent request sessions for same client: original and resumed stream
- Client-side SSE delivered chunks up to a point; terminal event never arrives in affected cases
- No 5xx from serving runtime; no auth failures

Expected behavior:
- Resumed stream should present stitched tokens including final terminal event and metadata

Relevant logs / snippets:
- Serving runtime trace (partial): 
  [2026-03-10T14:23:11Z] request_id=abc123 stream_session=cs-942: token_stream: ... "Thank you."
  [2026-03-10T14:23:11Z] request_id=abc123 stream_session=cs-942: choice.finish_reason=stop
- Edge-proxy combined log (adjacent sessions):
  203.12.45.9 - - [10/Mar/2026:14:23:11 +0000] "GET /v1/streams/?session=cs-942 HTTP/1.1" 200 - "-" "SSE-client"
  203.12.45.9 - - [10/Mar/2026:14:23:11 +0000] "GET /v1/streams/?session=cs-942 HTTP/1.1" 200 - "-" "SSE-client"
- Browser console (customer) shows last event ID changed and then no "end" event

Notes:
- Customer reproduces reliably when a TCP-level connection reuse / coalescence event occurs in the edge (observed when two short requests land on same HTTP/2 connection that the proxy reuses). This ticket uses the shorthand "edge connection coalescence" to describe the event where the proxy bundles stream fragments from resumed session onto the same upstream connection and we suspect an ordering or flush boundary gets lost.

investigation:
Summary of findings:
- Reproducible locally with HTTP/2 connection reuse and immediate client reconnect.
- Serving runtime always generates the full token stream and terminal metadata; stacktrace shows no errors.
- Edge-proxy shows two sequential GETs with same session token; when proxy reuses the upstream connection the final write sometimes remains in proxy internal write buffer and is never flushed to the downstream client before the proxied connection is closed by the client.

Hypotheses tested:
1) Parser bug in client SDK - ruled out (browser console shows no parse error; alternative clients show same behavior).
2) Serving runtime not emitting terminal event - ruled out by server traces.
3) Proxy write-coalescing + connection close race - likely. Reproduced by toggling proxy write_coalesce settings.

Next steps being executed:
- Edge-proxy change: add explicit flush boundary when terminal metadata is written upstream (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/311).
- Add metric to detect "stream-final-event-sent" vs "stream-final-event-delivered" to quantify impact across fleet.
- Schedule canary rollout to 10% of edge hosts for 48 hours and monitor stream-final delivery rate.

Links:
- Error analytics dash (internal): https://redwood.internal/dashboards/stream-finalization?team=support
- Edge proxy PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/311
resolution:
Workaround applied: recommended customer enable jittered reconnect delay (200–400 ms) and flipped dedicated-edge feature flag to disable http2 stream reuse for their tenant.
Fix in progress: edge-proxy PR adds explicit flush after terminal write and a write-boundary marker so coalesced writes no longer hide terminal fragments. Canaries scheduled; if canary is green will promote to prod.
Follow-ups:
- Post-deploy: run automated regression with 1000 simulated reconnects for each edge host to validate no regression in throughput/latency.
- Instrumentation: add cross-service counter for final-token-emitted vs final-token-acked and alert if delta > 0.1% for 24h.
- Customer follow-up: Confirm clipstream reports restored behavior once their tenant is on canary hosts.
